body: Chief: NEW TOPIC 'lexical-features' at the owner's request - porting ~/code/wordfeatures (imageability, Lancaster sensorimotor) to Scala. I read the R package rather than proposing from its name. HEADLINE FACTS: the model is glmnet - REGULARIZED LINEAR REGRESSION - so it ports as a coefficient vector and an intercept evaluated as a dot product against a ValidatedVector; no runtime, no ONNX. But inference needs an EMBEDDING from OpenAI or Google, and the sensorimotor model is embeddings-only, so the port is A DECODER OVER AN EXISTING EMBEDDING SPACE and it lands on RemotePolicy/AuthorizedRemoteRequest/PseudonymizedText - the apparatus we hardened tonight. THE DESIGN QUESTION IS TONIGHT'S DISEASE ARRIVING PROSPECTIVELY: the package ships HUMAN NORMS (Glasgow, Lancaster, MRC - measurements) AND a predictor for unseen words (estimates), and A NORMED VALUE AND A PREDICTED VALUE MUST NOT SHARE A FIELD. Our vocabulary already anticipates it - MissingReason.NotInLexicon exists in features/estimate.scala. And the R package is already scrupulous: its own doc says the model estimates human ratings from a frozen representation and does not claim the embedding has the property. Four questions open on the topic, including whether a PREDICTED sensorimotor profile is admissible as d_sens input at all - a cost term that decides which alignment wins, fed by a model's guess about a word, is a bigger claim than it looks. No bead filed; argue the shape first.
